_comment: THE one supply-chain advisory allowlist (scripts/audit-gate.mjs and apps/web/scripts/npm-audit-gate-smoke.ts both read it). Each entry is an npm-audit advisory accepted after triage, with the reason and the date of that triage. The gate fails on: any moderate/high/critical advisory not listed here; any listed advisory npm no longer reports (remove it); any advisory npm can fix without a major version change (update instead); and when the audit cannot run.

_categories.dev-build-only: Dev/build/test tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node.
_categories.not-reachable: Shipped, but the vulnerable code path cannot be reached with outside input in Morphit's use (the reason names the path).
_categories.runtime-accepted: Shipped and reachable in principle; the exposure is bounded as the reason says. No fix exists without a major version change. Patch when one lands.

GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g.title: qs: Denial of Service via Attacker Controlled isBuffer
GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g.rationale: Only qs 6.5.5 under request (matrix-bot -> matrix-bot-sdk -> request), the Matrix alert bot's HTTP client, is affected; express (4.22.3, installed by matrix-bot-sdk) and the MCP SDK's express 5 now resolve qs 6.16.1, outside the advisory. request only builds and merges query strings for the bot's own calls to the operator-configured homeserver; no Morphit code starts an express app (the MCP server is a plain node:http server) and no outside request reaches request's qs. matrix-bot-sdk's latest still depends on request, so no in-range update exists; replacing the SDK's HTTP layer is the way out.

GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9.rationale: Dev/test/build tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node (nodes serve the prebuilt frontend). Dev server only.

GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22.title: Vite: Files outside `server.fs.allow` could be served when project paths match system paths on non-Windows machine
GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22.rationale: Dev/test/build tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node (nodes serve the prebuilt frontend). `server.fs.allow` is enforced only by the Vite DEV server (`vite dev`, which CI never starts; vitest and `vite build` do not serve files). Vite 5.4.21 is the newest 5.x; the fix is in Vite 6.4.4 and later, a major upgrade tied to SvelteKit and vitest 2.

It is launch-editor bundled inside Vite, reached only through the Vite DEV server's /__open-in-editor endpoint (`vite dev`, which CI never starts; vitest and `vite build` do not serve it). GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3.title: Tinypool: Prototype Pollution gadget in worker options leads to Remote Code Execution
GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3.rationale: tinypool 1.1.1 is vitest's worker pool (a devDependency): it runs only during `vitest run` in development and CI, never on a node. The gadget needs an attacker to control vitest's worker options or pollute Object.prototype in the test process, which only our own test code configures. The fix is vitest 5 (a major); patch with that upgrade.

GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp.title: When Vitest UI server is listening, arbitrary file can be read and executed
GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp.rationale: Dev/test/build tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node (nodes serve the prebuilt frontend). Morphit never starts the Vitest UI (no @vitest/ui; only `vitest run`).

GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99.title: esbuild enables any website to send any requests to the development server and read the response
GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99.rationale: Affected copies: esbuild 0.19.12 at the top level and vite's 0.21.5 (dev). The top-level copy is apps/ops-cli's own devDependency pin (^0.19.12), used only by apps/ops-cli/scripts/build.mjs through build(); svelte-i18n 4.0.1 also declares ^0.19.2, but its shipped dist (cli.js, runtime) never loads esbuild. tsx's copy (0.28.2), the one that transpiles TypeScript on nodes, is outside the advisory range. The advisory needs esbuild's serve (dev server) mode, which nothing here starts; Vite's dev server is local development only. Raising the ops-cli pin would not clear it (svelte-i18n keeps 0.19.x; tried 2026-10-06), so the fix is a svelte-i18n release on a newer esbuild.

GHSA-72xf-g2v4-qvf3.title: tough-cookie Prototype Pollution vulnerability
GHSA-72xf-g2v4-qvf3.rationale: Reached only through the Matrix alert bot (matrix-bot → matrix-bot-sdk → request/request-promise), which talks only to the operator-configured homeserver: no user-controlled URL, cookie, form field or header reaches it. matrix-bot-sdk's latest still depends on request, so no in-range update exists; replacing the SDK's HTTP layer is the way out. Cookies come only from the operator's homeserver.

GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9.title: Vitest: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via @vitest/mocker Redirect Mock
GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9.rationale: Dev/test/build tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node (nodes serve the prebuilt frontend). Triggers only while running a test suite with attacker-supplied mock redirects; Morphit's tests control their own mocks.

GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr.title: Tinypool: Prototype Pollution Gadget to RCE in run() options
GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr.rationale: Same package and same exposure as GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3: tinypool runs only inside `vitest run` (development and CI), with run() options our own test setup passes; no node runs it and no outside input reaches it. The fix is vitest 5 (a major); patch with that upgrade.

GHSA-fjxv-7rqg-78g4.rationale: Reached only through the Matrix alert bot (matrix-bot → matrix-bot-sdk → request/request-promise), which talks only to the operator-configured homeserver: no user-controlled URL, cookie, form field or header reaches it. matrix-bot-sdk's latest still depends on request, so no in-range update exists; replacing the SDK's HTTP layer is the way out. A predictable multipart boundary matters only for attacker-influenced multipart bodies; the bot sends none.

The bot builds its own field names; none come from outside.

The SSRF needs an attacker-chosen URL or redirect target; the homeserver is the operator's own choice.

GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x.rationale: cookie 0.6 under @sveltejs/kit 2, used at build time only (the frontend is prerendered with adapter-static; nodes serve static files). The fix needs SvelteKit 3 (a major).

GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3.title: launch-editor: NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC path handling on Windows
GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3.rationale: Dev/test/build tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node (nodes serve the prebuilt frontend). The dev server's open-in-editor helper, Windows only.

GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq.title: uuid: Missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided
GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq.rationale: Reached only through the Matrix alert bot (matrix-bot → matrix-bot-sdk → request/request-promise), which talks only to the operator-configured homeserver: no user-controlled URL, cookie, form field or header reaches it. matrix-bot-sdk's latest still depends on request, so no in-range update exists; replacing the SDK's HTTP layer is the way out. request calls uuid v4 without a caller buffer; the v3/v5/v6 buffer path is never used.

GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8.title: Vitest: Code injection via unauthenticated manual mock registration
GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8.rationale: Dev/test tooling only; never shipped to or run on a node. The mock-registration endpoint belongs to Vitest's own server (browser mode / UI), which Morphit's test runs never start: vitest runs in node and jsdom environments only. The fix is in vitest 4.1.12 and later; the repo is on vitest 2.1.x (SvelteKit and Vite 5), so it needs the same major upgrade as the Vite advisories above.

GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5.title: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5.rationale: Zod 3.25.76 (indexer, relay, MCP server, matrix bot; and inside @session.js/client and the MCP SDK). The advisory needs an array schema WITHOUT a length bound fed outside input: zod then collects an issue per failing element without limit. Every zod array schema Morphit applies to outside input is bounded: indexer /v1/broadcast operations .max(10), signatures .max(8), extensions .max(16) (bounded in v1.21.15 for this advisory; test/api/broadcastLocalDeliver.test.ts), relay push muted_categories .max(3), relay create account_auths .max(0) / key_auths .length(1); request bodies are size-capped before parsing. @session.js/client's only zod schema is a number (its poll interval); the MCP SDK's schemas parse a local client's tool calls. No zod 3 release fixes it; the fix line is zod 4.6.6, a major upgrade across four apps.

GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f.title: @hono/node-server: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths
GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f.rationale: Only `serveStatic` (the separate `@hono/node-server/serve-static` export) is affected. Morphit imports only `serve` from @hono/node-server (apps/indexer/src/main.ts, apps/relay/src/main.ts); nothing imports serveStatic, and the MCP SDK, which also depends on the package, never references it (the MCP server is a plain node:http server). The indexer and relay serve no static files through Hono (the frontend is served prebuilt by the web server). The fix is in 2.1.3 and later, a major upgrade.
